# Grill me

Interview the user only about decisions that are theirs, so the work rests on settled choices. A routine choice is safe, reversible and inside the Assignment: make it yourself.

- Settle facts first: have a specialist read the repository or documentation, and reread what the user said. A question the code could have answered costs their attention for nothing.
- Ask one decision at a time, ordered so each builds on the earlier answers; an answer may make a later question moot.
- Write for someone outside the code: plain words, no internal terms or ids. Each question gives the options, what each leads to in concrete terms (the screen, the command, the visible result), and your recommended option first with the reason.
- Use AskUserQuestion when available, otherwise a short text question. Continue independent work while waiting.
- If the user does not answer or is busy, proceed on the recommended default and say so.
- Record each decision in the Intent: `intent update --material` with the revised requirements, folding the decision and its reason into the existing text. The revision moves, so reassess Assignments planned on the old one.

Stop when the decisions are settled or the user says to, give a short summary, and continue against the new revision.
